[1/4] Speed the app without tuning: in-process JS syntax check, memoized GPU detection, Rust GGUF header guard with JS fallback

impact_assessment.why: User directive to improve ModelDuck app speed (explicitly not tuning); measured 47ms spawn per JS syntax check, a 500 /api/gpu endpoint, and 6.4ms+ GGUF header validation on a synthetic large header
impact_assessment.benefits: No process spawn per syntax check, repeatable GPU info without re-import, and a native bounded GGUF header scan that scales to real vocabularies
impact_assessment.risks: contract: judge verdicts, API shapes and guard reject reasons must stay identical; dependency: Rust stdlib only and Node stdlib only, no new npm packages; concurrency: GGUF guard is called by scans and must remain bounded; state: no settings, prompts or generation paths are touched
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for each path, keep the JS guard as a fallback, compare verdicts on the same fixtures, run npm test and the project gates before each commit

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Speed tuning/engine tests without running a whole tune: make a failed llama-server spawn refuse immediately instead of waiting the 5s exit timeout

impact_assessment.why: User directive to look at tuning speed via tests only; TAP profile showed one engine test taking 5131ms because stop() waited 5s for an exit event that a failed spawn never emits
impact_assessment.benefits: Immediate actionable failure for a missing engine binary in the app, and a ~20% faster full test suite
impact_assessment.risks: contract: refusal code, Why/Fix text and exit-listener cleanup must stay identical; dependency: Node stdlib only; concurrency: the child-gone flag is per backend instance; state: no tuning settings, prompts or suite hashes change
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first timing test plus all 35 external-engine tests, then npm test and project gates
